body: **2026-10-04-the-wheel** — the tui wheel boundary: a closed non-editing set, and the wheel probed by exit 13 for the driver and exit 10 for the human. Clearing turn-running on an API-error end must not blur `not-delivered` (13) and `human-typing` (10, contract/cli-exit-codes/10): the wheel's holder and its turn state stay separate.

**2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint** — the readiness gate's 8.5 s bound falls on the driver only, and a human key during the gate wait wins (`send_under_the_paste_hint_a_human_key_during_the_gate_wait_wins`, sequenced on records, never a timer). This is the guard of decision/human-key-takes-the-wheel and decision/boundary-tests-sequenced-on-records. The "next send accepted" after an API-error end still passes this gate, and a new test must be sequenced on log records too.

**2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive** — the first live takeover reading, supplemental and never gating. It is the precedent behind decision/live-readings-never-gate, which applies to any live `claude` reading this chunk asks for.

**2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola** — the second live takeover reading on claude 2.1.296: `wheel{human}`, then send exit 10, then `release` back to the driver. Live readings stay never-gating. This is the same host and CLI line where the API-error defect was measured, and it is how a live reading is recorded without gating.

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** — a start made by a passed `viola revive` enters the same TUI passthrough boundary (decision/single-vendor-content-boundary, decision/human-keystrokes-never-blocked). The API-error turn-end path covers a revived start too.

**2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board** — the STATUS words `idle` / `busy` are printed words with no SGR. This is the basis of decision/state-carried-by-printed-word. After the turn end the board must read `idle` by its word, with no new colour-only state.

**2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers** — the MCP `wait` cap, `WAIT_CAP` of 50 s, falls on the driver only. A `wait` on the turn end must now return on the API-error end, not run out to its cap or the caller's timeout (contract/viola-wait/timed-out: true only for a caller-passed timeout).

**2026-10-18-compact-post-condition-ledger-row** — the confirm windows (10 s fallback, 40 s compact) are driver-only bounds, listed in decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver. The next send after the API-error end runs under them unchanged, and no new bound may fall on the human.

**2026-10-19-dialog-hold-for-the-driver** — the hold's end appends one `dialog-expired` line that wakes `wait`. This is a precedent for a new event line that ends a wait, and the API-error `turn-ended` path should follow the same form. The hold bounds the driver, never the human.

**2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame** — (the plugin against an impostor wrapper) a hook event or dialog call that meets a server other than the recorded wrapper sends no frame and fails open: exit 0, empty streams, under 1.0 s. That is contract/hook-call/server-verify-failed. A newly registered StopFailure-class hook call must go through the same shared `connect` and fail open the same way.

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** — (the plugin against a strict-modes-refused instance) a refused hook call exits 0 at once: no `config.json` read, no stdin read, no frame, no line. That is contract/hook-call/strict-modes-failed. The new hook arm's payload read must sit behind this check, and it stays not-assertable (decision/no-assertions-for-plugin-and-ipc).

**2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary** — after a contained feed panic the driver's `send` is refused `not-delivered` (exit 13) while a human key still reaches the child, and no viola literal reaches the outer terminal. This is a precedent for an exit-13 driver refusal that leaves the human untouched. The API-error defect is an unwanted exit-13 `turn-running` refusal.

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** — the closest precedent for this chunk's closed cause set. A peer's value is screened by `viola_core::is_code_word` (contract/code-word/format), and anything outside it reads a fixed fallback (`unknown`, or `wrapper fault` for a fault). `unknown`'s detail is a code word or nothing. The `--json` failure documents are clean (decision/json-failure-documents-are-clean, contract/cli-json-failure/document). The census of error writers and `thiserror_messages_interpolate_nothing` stand (decision/error-bodies-have-writer-and-witness, decision/thiserror-messages-interpolate-nothing). Mapping the CLI `error` string to a closed cause, with a fixed fallback member and no error text in any line, extends this register.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** — the closed cause words in exit 21's `detail` (and MCP's `isError` body), with `endpoint-lost` and `instance-dead` told apart. It also added the exit-cause table `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` (fake-agent) with `no_two_codes_share_a_hint`. This is the model of a closed viola-owned cause set with every member named, and a new cause word must not collide with these or reach the human as free text (decision/error-word-detail-hint).

**2026-11-01-unix-endpoint-and-home-hardening** — (hook and MCP on a refused socket directory) a hook call fails open with its one record, a `hook-decision` at WARN with `detail` `socket-dir-refused`. That is contract/hook-call/socket-dir-refused. A new hook registration inherits this fail-open behaviour and record form.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — the tui boundary is on openpty alone, and each of the three boundary clauses is its own nextest case on `ubuntu-latest` inside the `coverage` suite. That is where this chunk's a11y-relevant cases run (decision/boundary-tests-sequenced-on-records).

**2026-11-06-version-done-check** — the cli checks moved to `std::process::Command` with literal pins (the guard of decision/c0-c1-escaped, decision/linear-static-output, decision/send-refused-while-human-typing). The typed exit codes 10–14, 20 and 21 are pinned by literal asserts, and the outer-PTY driver is portable-pty `=0.9.0` (decision/portable-pty-outer-pty-driver). Any new test of the accepted next send or the refusal codes follows this form.
**2026-11-12T03-23-49-rows** — the master became rows, and every picked row was verified against the code at that point. It is the baseline the handles in the rows file are read against.

**2026-11-13-verify-readiness-on-the-input-box** — `~ decision/no-screen-content-parsing`: the vendor screen is parsed only for compiled signatures, and the prompt row only for its opening char. If this chunk ends the turn from the API-error text, it must come from the hook payload or the transcript, never from screen text. The text itself never reaches a line.

**2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed** — `~ contract/cli-exit-codes/11` (retired, never reused; an older wrapper's `budget-paused` reads `unknown` 14), plus `~ decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver`, `~ decision/time-bounds-never-on-human` and `~ decision/state-carried-by-printed-word` (`budget-paused` dropped). This is a recent precedent for retiring a code without reuse and for keeping a closed set's fallback stable across mixed binary versions.

**2026-11-14-status-line-interception-removed** — `~ decision/time-bounds-never-on-human` and `~ decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver` (the statusline deadline dropped). `− contract/viola-hook-statusline/exit`: the word is now an unknown hook event, its exit standing in architecture's hook-to-kind map. Registering a new hook event in `plugin/hooks/hooks.json` moves a word from unknown to known in that same map.

After that turn end the instance reads idle on viola list and the board, the turn-running state clears as a Stop clears it, a wait on the turn end returns, and the next send is accepted with no human pause and release.
It registers the CLI hook that ends such a turn, reads its payload in the Claude agent crate, maps the CLI error string into the neutral cause set with a fixed fallback member, and lets the fake agent emit that end.
It adds a test driving the API-error end through the fake agent and recorded or synthetic payloads that fails on the tree before the fix; P3 re-reads the defect from the code (which state reads turn-running while the board reads idle).

body: The turn-ended event line gains a cause key whose value is a code word from a closed set, with a fixed fallback member for any CLI value outside it; the cause value follows the code-word format.
The CLI's error text (the last assistant message and error details of an API-error end) is vendor content: it never reaches an event line, a snapshot or a log line; only the mapped code word does.
Vendor strings are screened to code words at the single vendor-content boundary: the CLI error string maps to a viola code word in the Claude agent crate and is never printed or logged as-is.
No error message the chunk adds interpolates the vendor's text; any new error type's message interpolates nothing and no bare status or vendor string stands as error text.
viola list and the board read the instance's state by its printed word idle after an API-error turn end, the same word a Stop-ended turn shows.

viola send after an API-error turn end is accepted; the exit-13 refusal and its turn-running reason code no longer fall on a send after such an end, while the refusal itself, its unable line, reason code and hint stay as they are for a turn still running.

viola wait on a turn end returns when the turn ends on an API error, so its waiting line is followed by its result rather than hanging until timed_out; time bounds stay on the driver, never on the human.
The human never needs pause and release to recover the wheel after an API-error end; human keystrokes stay never blocked and the human taking the wheel behaves as before.
The turn end is read from the hook payload, a record, never by parsing the claude screen content or inspecting claude's content beyond signatures.
The new guard test runs on the fake agent and recorded or synthetic payloads; a live claude reading never gates the build, and none is started without the operator's cap.
An unknown or unlisted cause stays visible as the fixed fallback code word rather than being dropped or replaced by the CLI's string.
A test socket the new test opens lives under the short tmp root, and readers of event lines skip and count unknown data keys so mixed binary versions stay readable.

body: A new hook registration in the plugin for the API-error turn-end signal: exec-form command hook, its hook tier (async, or the sync ordering spine with no reply body), its row in the hook-to-kind map beside Stop, and its hook subcommand name joining the register of hook names.

The hook binary's behaviour on the new hook: fails open, never writes stderr, exits 0 with no body, exits silently with no trusted instance, stays inside the hook connect and spine deadline, and loses the event rather than the turn when the endpoint is lost.

The API-error payload read in viola-agent-claude, the only crate that knows Claude shapes: parsed tolerantly, the CLI's error string mapped into the closed cause set, a value outside it reading a fixed fallback member (unparseable external values become unknown), and the crate doing no file I/O.

The cause set's neutral home in viola-core: a closed set with every member named, no Claude-specific name, added only in viola-core per the agent-neutral event-kind rule, its wire values kebab-case enum strings, and the root bin consuming only the normalised event.

The turn-ended event data contract: a new cause key beside last_assistant_message and background_tasks — a wire-contract change to Standard Contracts — under the event line shape, snake_case field names, absent optional fields omitted, and the normalised event kinds list.

Mixed-version tolerance for the new key: readers skip and count unknown data keys, missing reads as null, so older and newer binaries keep reading the same events log; whether the change bumps the protocol version follows the protocol-version bump rule.

The error text never leaves as data: last_assistant_message and error_details on this path reach no events.ndjson line, no snapshot and no process-log line — upstream text is untrusted content, process logs hold codes only, and content-bearing detail lives only in the instance detail file.

The wheel and send path after the API-error end: the turn-running state cleared exactly as a Stop clears it, so the next driver send is not refused not-delivered turn-running (CLI exit 13) and a send is still refused, never queued, while a turn truly runs.
The channel wait method: a wait on the turn end wakes and returns on the API-error turn-ended event, through the blocking wait (nothing polls), its start offset and timeout unchanged.

The board (viola list and MCP list) and the instance snapshot read idle after the API-error end, with the snapshot replay agreeing with the live state and the instance snapshot carrying no error text.

The fake agent's ability to emit the API-error end through its test seams, with recorded or synthetic payloads; a synthetic payload scrubbed like a recorded fixture and named as a probe capture payload file; no live claude in CI and tests run against the fake agent.

A dependence on undocumented claude behaviour (whether the StopFailure-class hook fires live for every API-error end) is ruled by the capability ledger as the single gate for CLI behaviour, with a viola verify probe; whether a new row is added and how it is probed is decided at P3/P4.

A live claude start is not given: real CLI probes run only locally, and any needed live reading is a counted fork asked before the card; a home given to verify --record goes through the recorded-fixture home helper, fixtures recorded only from a clean verify.
The new guard test fails on the tree before the fix and carries a one-off remove-the-guard control under a kill deadline, named by the test's name alone; no mutation run, local or dispatched.
A rate-limit or billing cause read on the turn end is a logged code only: it opens no usage-budget gate, no budget state, and no send paused or refused on usage.

Error handling in the new code: typed thiserror errors per crate whose messages interpolate nothing, anyhow only in the root bin, error chains only in the detail file, events emitted only through the one obs event emitter.

body: The turn-ended event written to the instance event log on an API-error turn end: its event line format and keys, and a cause value from a closed set in its data.

The turn-ended event data keys: today exactly last_assistant_message and background_tasks; adding a cause key changes the event data contract, and readers that meet an unknown key skip and count it, so mixed binary versions stay readable.
The closed cause set: every member named, a CLI error string outside it mapped to one fixed fallback member, never passed through; a closed set changes only by a recorded decision.

Where the cause set lives: a neutral home in the core crate with no Claude-specific name, per the event-kind rule; the mapping from the CLI's error string lives only in the Claude agent crate, the one crate that knows Claude.

The error text (last_assistant_message and error_details on this path) reaches no event line, no snapshot and no process log line: logs carry no secrets, errors are sanitized at every surface, role logs carry codes only, and the absence is proven by a probe against the plan's test names and fixture keys; whether either reaches the content-bearing detail tier is left to P3/P4 under the never-log floor.
The instance state after the API-error end: the board and viola list --json read idle, the same state send reads, never idle on the board while send still holds turn-running.

viola send after the API-error end is accepted and confirmed, not refused not-delivered turn-running with exit 13; send refusal order and the turn-running refusal stay as they are for a turn still running.
viola wait and the channel wait method wake on the API-error turn-ended record, including when it is already past the cursor; a waiter on the turn end returns.
The wheel after the API-error end: turn-running cleared exactly as a Stop clears it, no human pause and release needed, and the wheel's driver kept.

The new hook entry point of viola hook: exec-form entry, exit code, empty stdout, stderr and deadline as every hook verb; hooks fail open; unknown payload fields tolerated; the instance check comes first; a hook outside a wrapped session is a silent no-op; the hook never writes a frame to an impostor server.

The hook payload reader for the StopFailure-class payload (error, optional error_details, optional last_assistant_message): a bounded reader with no unbounded JSON depth, a parser surface under property tests.

The fake agent firing the API-error hook on a step: its fired events, hook execution with its stdin payload, script format and control-file gating; the fake agent stands in for claude at that boundary.

No recorded fixture holds a StopFailure payload: the test uses synthetic payloads carrying a canary, named by hook event and checked against the tolerant fixture schema; fixtures stay free of real data and none is hand-written as product state.

A dependence on undocumented claude behaviour (whether StopFailure fires for every API-error end) is a capability-ledger row with a viola verify probe; a fake-agent run is no proof of real-CLI behaviour.

No live claude start without the cap asked first: tests run on the fake agent only, real claude never in CI, live readings are not a test layer, and a needed live reading is a counted request through the overseer.

The new test must fail on the tree before the fix, and each new guard test carries a bounded remove-the-guard witness run through the gate control under a kill deadline, its case the test's name alone.
No mutation run, local or dispatched, for this chunk; mutation testing stays off CI and outside this chunk's proof.
The end-to-end proof over the real viola hook and fake agent asserts on logged events and the list document, never on the child's screen; waits key on logged events, never on sleeps.
Test sockets go under the short /tmp root and any home given to verify --record goes through record_home(); every test makes its own private home.
The hook performance budget for spine hooks and the hook deadline bind the new hook verb if it joins the spine; a fire-and-forget hook still answers within the hook deadline.
